blocking_issues_v3: AC15 is UNSATISFIABLE as written. It requires 'a dedicated test asserts the SQL-computed floor equals commercial_authority_v2.window_floor(now) for at least one Feb-29-anchored fixture'. window_floor is a function of `now` alone, but Scope IN sanctions exactly two SQL objects and forbids window arithmetic in both (contract_contracting_date_v1: 'no CURRENT_DATE - precedence resolution only'). Substantively tighter here (local main is stale by hundreds of files; merge-base(origin/main,HEAD) == HEAD~1), documented in the test docstring, but it is a deviation from the AC's literal text.

Scope IN asked for GRANT SELECT to the read-only role used by 098/101. The migration uses REVOKE <DML> ... FROM PUBLIC + GRANT SELECT ... TO PUBLIC, which is exactly 101's pattern and subsumes the named role used only by 098. No security regression; naming smartlic_public_reader explicitly would match 098 more closely.

AC18's secondary test brackets a bare SELECT count(*) between two identical QUALIFICATION_SQL runs in one transaction, so it cannot detect a migration-induced membership change even in principle. It does add value (non-vacuous fixture, asserts pg_get_viewdef of v_contracts_canonical_v2 references none of the 4 new objects). AC18 is carried by the structural proof, as the story itself pre-declares; report kept honest.
